questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should keep when driving behind a motorcycle in normal weather and traffic?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three to four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three to four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep three to four seconds of distance between you and a motorcycle. This gives you time to react if the rider falls or stops suddenly. The extra distance helps you avoid hitting the rider.

questions.question: If an oncoming car has bright headlights that blind you, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded until the car passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink if you will drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
You are approaching a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down at unmarked railroad crossings and be ready to stop. Look both ways for trains before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance from the tracks and wait for it to pass.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for one hour or longer.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. The water brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat causes more oil to rise to the road.

questions.question: What speed should you always travel at?

options.text: The speed of the vehicles around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that matches road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that matches road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match the road conditions, weather, and legal speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop.
Fines are doubled in a work zone.
Stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and prepare you for hazards ahead. This sign tells you to watch for bicycles crossing the road.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Press hard on the brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and pull off the road to safety.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Be very alert for children and pedestrians when you see these signs.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?

options.text: Red.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They alert you to possible dangers on the road.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up next to the car in front of your desired parking space.
Back slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up next to the car in front of your desired parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a parking space and signaling, stop parallel to the car in front of the empty space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line next to your lane, when may you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
If you are on an expressway.
If the road ahead is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you can cross it to pass. Only pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as the traffic.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as the traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic. Vehicles moving at the same speed are less likely to crash. Accidents happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross it to pass. You may pass on the left if the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check for traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you spot vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic. Signal, look for an opening, then merge smoothly into traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Go—you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway road or shoulder. Other drivers do not expect this and a crash will likely happen. Continue to the next exit instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School zone or crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: The maximum speed limit.
A speed that is faster than is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must not drive faster than is reasonable and safe. You must drive at a speed that fits the area, traffic type and condition, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and light. You must also stay within legal speed limits.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to cross traffic that could cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to cross traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed and let crossing or merging vehicles go first. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four-way intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
A divided highway is starting.
A divided highway is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is ending.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the divided highway ends ahead. Get ready to change lanes or move to a different position.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill on a street without a curb or when parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, keep a minimum distance of:

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: More distance between your vehicle and others gives you more time to react. Keep a minimum distance of two seconds in normal weather and traffic. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: You must pull over and let an emergency vehicle pass:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether it is coming from behind you or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires you to use the oncoming traffic lane to complete your pass. Only pass if you can do so safely and legally.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants left. This means:

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will have to turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge marks the boundary between the travel lane and shoulder. When the edge line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.
